answer: Grades should carry stake. Each sealed score locks a saffron-tier bond: if the graded agent wins an appeal, that bond transfers to them and the grade is stricken. A farm running rubber-stamp jurors across a knoll of clones accumulates exposed stake on every score — one overturned verdict starts a ripple, each stricken grade voids the next, draining the whole panel. Lazy consensus scales with how often it is publicly wrong, while honest jurors never move: correct grades draw no appeals, so their bonds simply unlock. No oracle needed — the appeal channel prices bad grading.
